title: Kestrel Dynamics — Capacity heuristics & prewarm scenario review
summary: Discovery focused on reserved GPU sizing, tenant isolation needs for regulated models, burst/pre-warm strategy, and tradeoffs between Dedicated and Hosted. Customer wants predictable p99 latency for inference, on-prem-like isolation for certain models, and a clear SLA for burst scenarios. Action items include provisioning a small benchmark run, security docs, and a follow-up pilot proposal.
action_items: Priya Raman: share model list + typical sequence lengths and 95/99 lat targets (due 2026-12-27)
Jonah Lee (Redwood): run a 2-hour micro-benchmark with 2x burst profile and share raw traces (due 2027-01-04)
Maya Patel: send pricing sheet for reserved pools + burst credit model (due 2026-12-22)
Carlos Mendes: provide VPC diagram and egress restrictions for private deployment review (due 2026-12-29)
Iris Chen: compile SOC2 + KMS + SSO integration docs and upload to shared folder (due 2026-12-23)
next_steps: Redwood to schedule micro-benchmark run (AE/SE + Kestrel infra)
Kestrel to upload model binaries and example inputs to secure dropbox link
Follow-up call in ~2 weeks to review benchmark results and pilot proposal
Redwood to propose reserved GPU sizing + burst credits option in proposal
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-20 16:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Recording started automatically
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (SE), Iris (SE), Tom (CS); Priya (Head of ML), Carlos (Infra), Luke (CTO), Samir (SRE), Zoe (Product)

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood Dedicated team. Jonah's gonna go deep on the capacity questions.
00:12 Priya: Thanks, Maya. We wanted to go through how you think about reserved GPU sizing, isolation for some of our sensitive models, and how burst works — we have unpredictable spikes during release cycles.
00:22 Jonah: cool. To kick off, can you give a sense of baseline QPS today and the p95/p99 you need? also sequence lengths — are most of these <512 tokens or longer?
00:35 Priya: Baseline right now is around 20 qps across a handful of models, the big one is gen-qa which averages about 800 tokens per request for full convo state, p95 is roughly 450ms but p99 is all over — 1.2 to 2.4s depending on concurrency and token lengths. during spikes we see bursts to 120 qps for 10-20 minutes.
01:02 Jonah: okay that helps. for Dedicated we usually size reserved pools to cover peak steady-state throughput you expect to commit to — then we layer a warm-pool / burst credit model to handle short spikes. question: do you have strict single-tenant isolation requirements for any of these models? or is logical isolation (namespaces + encryption) sufficient?
01:22 Luke: good question. for a couple of models used in financial vertical, legal wants network/isolation similar to on-prem — basically want tenant-dedicated instances for those models. for others, logical isolation is ok, but we need audit logs and ability to revoke keys quickly.
01:37 Maya: sounds like a mix. Redwood Dedicated supports node-level reservations (single-tenant) for sensitive workloads; that raises cost but gives the tenancy guarantee. we can carve out a small dedicated slice for the two models and keep the rest on multi-tenant reserved.
01:54 Priya: how does that work with pre-warm? if a model sits idle on a dedicated node, do you still get warm KV cache and low p99?
02:04 Jonah: yes, if you reserve nodes and pin model versions we can keep KV cache resident and pre-warm on startup. for true single-tenant nodes we can keep a warm-pool with prewarmed model artifacts and warmed kv caches; that costs more but is the lowest-latency option.
02:22 Samir: what's the typical cost of maintaining a warm pool for, say, one A100-equivalent node prewarmed 24/7? we're evaluating whether to rely on burst credit vs dedicated warm pools.
02:34 Maya: i'll send a granular cost bake-up, but rough rule: 24/7 warm pool is about 30-40% of the node's reserved cost depending on region/instance. burst credits (on top of reserved) are cheaper for infrequent spikes, but if spikes are daily or long, warm pools win on latency predictability.
02:56 Carlos: we also have constraints on egress and a locked-down VPC — can Redwood deploy a Dedicated control plane that integrates with our VPC and KMS?
03:06 Iris: yes, for Private we have VPC/subnet integration and KMS/HSM options; Dedicated can be deployed in a VPC with our private control plane too. for keys we support customer-managed KMS and key rotation. we'll share the integration doc.
03:20 Priya: SOC2 and audit logs — legal will need evidence.
03:26 Iris: we have SOC2 Type II reports and can expose audit logs per request. also RBAC and SSO via SAML/OIDC. i'll attach the security pack to the doc share.
03:38 Zoe: what about fallbacks — if your Dedicated pool is saturated during an insane spike, will Redwood fail open to Hosted? that's something the product team is worried about from an SLA perspective.
03:49 Jonah: we offer policy-driven routing. you can configure fallbacks: strict (fail requests), degraded (route to a smaller cheaper model), or fallback-to-hosted. fallback-to-hosted is possible but you need to agree on data handling for those requests — hosted means data may touch shared infrastructure unless you opt for dedicated-hosted tenancy.
04:12 Luke: we probably want restful fallback policies that preserve PII rules; for sensitive models fallback should be disallowed.
04:21 Priya: another question on model variants — can Redwood automatically fallback to quantized variants to save cost during spikes?
04:28 Jonah: yes, model variant routing is supported. runtime can switch to a lower-precision/quantized model with a defined quality threshold. we can run A/B tests to check quality delta.
04:38 Carlos: how do you measure p99 for planning? our ops team wants to tie capacity to observed p99 under production traces not synthetic TPS.
04:46 Jonah: ideal is to provide a representative trace — sequence length distribution, concurrency patterns. we'll run a replay on our benchmark harness and return p50/p95/p99 and token-cost numbers. that's what the micro-benchmark will do.
04:59 Priya: timeline — we want a pilot in January if benchmarks look good. realistic?
05:04 Maya: yes, pilot in Jan doable. we should align on deliverables: Kestrel provides models and traces, Redwood runs benchmark, then we propose reserved sizing + burst plan.
05:16 Samir: on SLAs — do you offer latency SLO guarantees for p95/p99 with reserved capacity?
05:22 Maya: our SLA focuses on availability and latency tiers for dedicated pools; we can offer latency objectives but p99 guarantees are scoped to config and customer-provided traces. enterprise SLA add-on possible.
05:34 Zoe: curious about prewarming time — if we do a canary deploy of a new model version, how long until it's warmed to p99 levels?
05:41 Jonah: depends on model size and KV cache priming — typically 2-8 minutes for a full KV warm on large models once you run a few warm requests; but with a warm pool we can reduce that to sub-60s.
05:55 Priya: do you have multi-region replication for failover? we need DR in EU and US.
06:02 Iris: yes we can route across regions and keep replica pools; there are added costs for cross-region replication and cold-starts during failover. we can design an active-passive for EU/US.
06:16 Luke: about billing — do you bill for warm pools as reserved nodes or as an extra line item?
06:23 Maya: typically warm pools are part of reserved pool sizing; we model it as partially reserved capacity in proposals, or as an add-on for dedicated warm pool hours. we'll show both in the pricing sheet.
06:34 Priya: security nuance — for some models we need HSM-backed key usage and separate audit trails. is that supported?
06:41 Iris: yes HSM/KMS integrations supported for Private/Dedicated deployments. separate audit trails can be configured and exported to your SIEM.
06:50 Carlos: any references for customers who've done similar hybrid: mixed dedicated for compliance models + multi-tenant for others?
06:57 Maya: yes, we'll share a case study — a fintech customer that left in obfuscated name — we have a anonymized deck showing reserved isolation plus warm-pool heuristics.
07:10 Zoe: what's the usual commit term for reserved GPUs? we prefer 6-12 months but need some flexibility.
07:17 Maya: standard is 12 month committed reservations with quarterly review; we can do 6 month pilot reservations for initial phase and convert to 12 if the pilot proves out.
07:26 Priya: ok. last operational Q — observability: can we get token-level cost and per-route latency breakdowns in your console?
07:33 Tom: yep, Redwood Console exposes per-model, per-route metrics, token breakdown and tracing hooks. we can integrate with your telemetry stack.
07:42 Luke: can we get a copy of your prewarm tuning guide? we've had weird perf cliffs when autoscaling kicks in.
07:48 Jonah: sure, we'll include prewarm knobs: batch size limits, KV pinning, kernel selection hints, and time-based prewarm policies.
07:57 Priya: great. those are most of our concerns. thanks.
08:00 Maya: quick recap — next steps: Kestrel shares model list and traces; Redwood schedules benchmark; Redwood sends pricing and security pack; follow-up in ~2 weeks. Any objections?
08:11 Priya: no objections. sounds good.
08:16 Luke: thanks everyone.
08:18 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites. recording stopped.
